Q: How to apply a geometric anisotropic filter 1/cos²(theta) to a raster? A:

This solution is based on the same question I posted on R-sig-Geo and one member kindly responded. His solution (which I share here) works perfectly (I tested it on many real world datasets):

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# =============================================================================
# anisotropic_blur_demo.R
#
# Spatially-varying 1-D Gaussian blur for downscaling VIIRS night-lights.
#
# The coarse -> fine transfer function is approximated by a Gaussian whose
# CROSS-TRACK (along-x) width grows with the per-pixel viewing angle theta:
#
#       sigma_x(theta) = sigma0 / cos(theta)^2          (sigma0 in pixels)
#
# Because theta is a function of the cross-track *column* only (constant down
# each column / along-track), the same 1-D operator blurs every row. That
# operator is a banded, column-stochastic matrix W, so the whole blur is a
# single (sparse) matrix multiply  X %*% Wx  instead of a per-pixel loop.
#
# OPTIONAL along-track (vertical, y) pooling -- see `pool_y` below -- is applied
# as a SEPARABLE second pass with a constant (angle-independent) kernel Wy:
#
#       out = Wy %*% ( X %*% Wx )
#
# Both passes are NA-aware: each output pixel is renormalized by the weight of
# the *valid* neighbours it actually saw, so swath edges and cloud/fill gaps
# are handled in one step (num / den) rather than propagated.
#
# Run:   Rscript anisotropic_blur_demo.R
# Figures are written to $ANISO_OUTDIR (default: a temp folder, path printed).
#
# Requires: terra, Matrix, ggplot2 (+ viridisLite for palettes).
# =============================================================================

suppressMessages({
  library(terra)
  library(Matrix)
  library(ggplot2)
})

set.seed(42)

OUTDIR <- Sys.getenv("ANISO_OUTDIR", unset = file.path("/Users/rodrigues.h/Desktop/Anisotropic", "anisotropic_demo"))

dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

banner <- function(txt) cat("\n", strrep("=", 78), "\n", txt, "\n",
                            strrep("=", 78), "\n", sep = "")


# =============================================================================
# 1.  THE FUNCTION
# =============================================================================

#' Anisotropic (angle-dependent) 1-D Gaussian blur of a raster.
#'
#' @param x        SpatRaster of values (e.g. a night-lights predictor).
#' @param theta    SpatRaster of per-pixel cross-track viewing angle, in
#'                 DEGREES, with the same dimensions as `x`. Assumed (and
#'                 collapsed) to be constant down each column.
#' @param sigma0   Cross-track Gaussian sd at nadir, in PIXEL units. The width
#'                 at column c is sigma_x = sigma0 / cos(theta_c)^2.
#' @param trunc    Kernel truncation, in multiples of sigma (half-width =
#'                 ceiling(trunc * sigma)). 3 keeps >99.7% of the mass.
#' @param pool_y   Optional ALONG-TRACK (vertical) pooling, applied as a
#'                 separable second pass with a constant kernel:
#'                   "none"     -> cross-track blur only (default; the PSF is
#'                                 purely horizontal, every row independent).
#'                   "gaussian" -> also blur down columns with a Gaussian of
#'                                 sd = `width_y` pixels.
#'                   "uniform"  -> also average down columns with a boxcar of
#'                                 half-height round(`width_y`) pixels (i.e.
#'                                 "pool all y within +/- width_y uniformly").
#' @param width_y  Along-track kernel scale in PIXELS (rows). Interpreted as the
#'                 Gaussian sd when pool_y = "gaussian", or the boxcar
#'                 half-height when pool_y = "uniform". Ignored for "none".
#'
#' @return A SpatRaster with the same geometry (ext/crs/dims) as `x`.
anisotropic_blur <- function(x, theta,
                             sigma0  = 10,
                             trunc   = 3,
                             pool_y  = c("none", "gaussian", "uniform"),
                             width_y = 0) {
  pool_y <- match.arg(pool_y)
  
  M  <- as.matrix(x, wide = TRUE)                                  # nr x nc
  th <- colMeans(as.matrix(theta, wide = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)      # one angle / column
  nr <- nrow(M); nc <- ncol(M)
  
  ## ---- cross-track kernel Wx: banded, column-varying sigma (UN-normalized) ----
  sigma_x <- sigma0 / cos(th * pi / 180)^2
  Gx <- .band_varying(nc, sigma = sigma_x, h = ceiling(trunc * sigma_x))
  
  ## ---- along-track kernel Wy: banded, constant (UN-normalized) ----
  Gy <- switch(pool_y,
               none     = Diagonal(nr),                                       # identity -> x-only
               gaussian = {
                 if (width_y <= 0) stop("pool_y='gaussian' requires width_y > 0 (sd in pixels)")
                 .band_const(nr, h = ceiling(trunc * width_y), sd = width_y, shape = "gaussian")
               },
               uniform  = {
                 if (width_y <= 0) stop("pool_y='uniform' requires width_y > 0 (half-height in pixels)")
                 .band_const(nr, h = round(width_y),            sd = NA,      shape = "uniform")
               })
  
  ## ---- NA-aware separable blur:  out = (Gy (M0 Gx)) / (Gy (mask Gx)) ----
  mask <- matrix(as.numeric(!is.na(M)), nr, nc)                    # 1 where valid
  M0   <- M; M0[mask == 0] <- 0
  num  <- Gy %*% (M0   %*% Gx)
  den  <- Gy %*% (mask %*% Gx)
  out  <- as.matrix(num / den)
  out[!is.finite(out)] <- NA                                       # all-NA window -> NA
  
  rast(out, extent = ext(x), crs = crs(x))
}

# Column-varying band: Gx[j, c] = exp(-0.5*((j-c)/sigma_c)^2) for |j-c| <= h_c.
# Applied on the RIGHT (X %*% Gx) so column c gathers from input columns j,
# using sigma at the central/output column c. Columns are normalized later via
# the num/den step, which also absorbs edge truncation.
.band_varying <- function(n, sigma, h) {
  ii <- jj <- xx <- vector("list", n)
  for (c in seq_len(n)) {
    j <- max(1L, c - h[c]):min(n, c + h[c])
    ii[[c]] <- j
    jj[[c]] <- rep.int(c, length(j))
    xx[[c]] <- exp(-0.5 * ((j - c) / sigma[c])^2)
  }
  sparseMatrix(i = unlist(ii), j = unlist(jj), x = unlist(xx), dims = c(n, n))
}

# Constant band (Gaussian or uniform), applied on the LEFT (Gy %*% Y).
.band_const <- function(n, h, sd, shape = c("gaussian", "uniform")) {
  shape <- match.arg(shape)
  h <- max(0L, as.integer(h))
  ii <- jj <- xx <- vector("list", n)
  for (r in seq_len(n)) {
    s <- max(1L, r - h):min(n, r + h)
    d <- s - r
    ii[[r]] <- rep.int(r, length(s))
    jj[[r]] <- s
    xx[[r]] <- if (shape == "gaussian") exp(-0.5 * (d / sd)^2) else rep.int(1, length(s))
  }
  sparseMatrix(i = unlist(ii), j = unlist(jj), x = unlist(xx), dims = c(n, n))
}


# =============================================================================
# 2.  HELPERS for the demo (pixel-unit rasters + ggplot theming)
# =============================================================================

# Wrap a matrix as a raster whose 1 cell = 1 pixel (square cells, no CRS).
pix_rast <- function(mat) {
  rast(mat, extent = ext(0, ncol(mat), 0, nrow(mat)), crs = "")
}

# Cross-track angle raster: theta varies along columns (x), constant down rows.
make_theta <- function(nr, nc, from_deg, to_deg) {
  th <- seq(from_deg, to_deg, length.out = nc)
  pix_rast(matrix(th, nrow = nr, ncol = nc, byrow = TRUE))
}

theme_night <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey12", colour = NA),
          plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "grey12", colour = NA),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "grey12", colour = NA),
          panel.grid       = element_blank(),
          strip.text       = element_text(colour = "grey90", face = "bold"),
          plot.title       = element_text(colour = "grey95", face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "grey75"),
          text             = element_text(colour = "grey90"),
          axis.text        = element_text(colour = "grey70"))
}

# Faceted raster plot from a named list of SpatRasters.
gg_panels <- function(rasters, title = "", subtitle = NULL, ncol = NULL, limits = NULL) {
  df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rasters), function(nm) {
    d <- as.data.frame(rasters[[nm]], xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)
    names(d)[3] <- "value"; d$panel <- nm; d
  }))
  df$panel <- factor(df$panel, levels = names(rasters))
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
    geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", na.value = "grey35", limits = limits) +
    coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = ncol %||% length(rasters)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "value") +
    theme_night()
}

save_fig <- function(p, file, w = 9, h = 4.5) {
  path <- file.path(OUTDIR, file)
  ggsave(path, p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 130, bg = "grey12")
  cat(sprintf("  saved  %s\n", path))
}


# =============================================================================
# 3.  REFERENCE implementations (only for validation)
# =============================================================================

# Your original idea: explicit per-pixel loop, cross-track only.
loop_blur_x <- function(M, theta_col, sigma0, trunc = 3) {
  nr <- nrow(M); nc <- ncol(M); out <- matrix(NA_real_, nr, nc)
  for (r in seq_len(nr)) for (c in seq_len(nc)) {
    sigma   <- sigma0 / cos(theta_col[c] * pi / 180)^2
    halfwin <- ceiling(trunc * sigma)
    idx <- max(1, c - halfwin):min(nc, c + halfwin)
    w <- exp(-0.5 * (abs(idx - c) / sigma)^2); w <- w / sum(w)
    out[r, c] <- sum(w * M[r, idx])
  }
  out
}

# Brute-force, NA-aware, separable 2-D reference (validates the pool_y feature).
loop_blur_2d <- function(M, theta_col, sigma0, trunc, width_y, shape_y) {
  nr <- nrow(M); nc <- ncol(M); out <- matrix(NA_real_, nr, nc)
  sx <- sigma0 / cos(theta_col * pi / 180)^2; hx <- ceiling(trunc * sx)
  hy <- if (shape_y == "gaussian") ceiling(trunc * width_y) else round(width_y)
  for (r in seq_len(nr)) for (c in seq_len(nc)) {
    is <- max(1, r - hy):min(nr, r + hy)
    js <- max(1, c - hx[c]):min(nc, c + hx[c])
    num <- 0; den <- 0
    for (s in is) {
      wy <- if (shape_y == "gaussian") exp(-0.5 * ((s - r) / width_y)^2) else 1
      for (j in js) {
        v <- M[s, j]; if (is.na(v)) next
        wx <- exp(-0.5 * ((j - c) / sx[c])^2)
        num <- num + wy * wx * v; den <- den + wy * wx
      }
    }
    out[r, c] <- if (den > 0) num / den else NA
  }
  out
}


# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE A -- correctness & speed
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE A  |  correctness vs reference loops, and speed")

# A1. cross-track only vs your loop (should match to machine precision)
nr <- 6; nc <- 150
M  <- matrix(runif(nr * nc), nr, nc)
th <- seq(10, 45, length.out = nc)
ref_x <- loop_blur_x(M, th, sigma0 = 8, trunc = 3)
got_x <- as.matrix(anisotropic_blur(pix_rast(M), make_theta(nr, nc, 10, 45),
                                    sigma0 = 8, pool_y = "none"), wide = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("A1  pool_y='none'      max|matrix - loop|     = %.2e\n",
            max(abs(ref_x - got_x))))

# A2. separable + NA, Gaussian along-track, vs brute-force 2-D loop
Mna <- M; Mna[2, 30:34] <- NA; Mna[5, 80] <- NA
ref_g <- loop_blur_2d(Mna, th, sigma0 = 8, trunc = 3, width_y = 2.5, shape_y = "gaussian")
got_g <- as.matrix(anisotropic_blur(pix_rast(Mna), make_theta(nr, nc, 10, 45),
                                    sigma0 = 8, pool_y = "gaussian", width_y = 2.5),
                   wide = TRUE)
ok <- is.finite(ref_g) & is.finite(got_g)
cat(sprintf("A2  pool_y='gaussian'  max|matrix - loop| (NA) = %.2e\n",
            max(abs(ref_g[ok] - got_g[ok]))))

# A3. separable + NA, uniform along-track, vs brute-force 2-D loop
ref_u <- loop_blur_2d(Mna, th, sigma0 = 8, trunc = 3, width_y = 3, shape_y = "uniform")
got_u <- as.matrix(anisotropic_blur(pix_rast(Mna), make_theta(nr, nc, 10, 45),
                                    sigma0 = 8, pool_y = "uniform", width_y = 3),
                   wide = TRUE)
ok <- is.finite(ref_u) & is.finite(got_u)
cat(sprintf("A3  pool_y='uniform'   max|matrix - loop| (NA) = %.2e\n",
            max(abs(ref_u[ok] - got_u[ok]))))

# A4. speed at a realistic granule size
bigM  <- matrix(runif(800 * 3200), 800, 3200)
bigTh <- make_theta(800, 3200, -56, 56)
bigR  <- pix_rast(bigM)
t_blur <- system.time(invisible(anisotropic_blur(bigR, bigTh, sigma0 = 10)))["elapsed"]
cat(sprintf("A4  800 x 3200 granule, sparse blur     = %.3f s\n", t_blur))

# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE B -- how sigma_x grows across the swath
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE B  |  sigma_x(theta) across the scan")

ncB <- 800
thetaB  <- seq(-56, 56, length.out = ncB)
sigma0B <- 10
dB <- data.frame(column = seq_len(ncB), theta = thetaB,
                 sigma  = sigma0B / cos(thetaB * pi / 180)^2)
pB <- ggplot(dB, aes(column, sigma, colour = abs(theta))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "|theta| (deg)") +
  labs(title = expression("Cross-track kernel width  " * sigma[x] == sigma[0] / cos^2 * theta),
       subtitle = sprintf("sigma0 = %g px ; nadir at swath centre, +/-56 deg at edges", sigma0B),
       x = "cross-track column", y = expression(sigma[x] * "  (pixels)")) +
  theme_night()
save_fig(pB, "fig1_sigma_swath.png", w = 8, h = 4)

# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE C -- anisotropy on identical bright bars + line-spread validation
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE C  |  identical bars smear more toward the swath edge")

nrC <- 120; ncC <- 360
bars <- c(45, 115, 185, 255, 325)
fieldC <- matrix(0, nrC, ncC)
fieldC[, bars] <- 1                          # 1-px vertical bars spanning all rows
xC  <- pix_rast(fieldC)
thC <- make_theta(nrC, ncC, 0, 64)
sigma0C <- 1.3
xC_blur <- anisotropic_blur(xC, thC, sigma0 = sigma0C, pool_y = "none")

save_fig(gg_panels(list("input (identical bars)" = xC, "anisotropic blur" = xC_blur),
                   title = "Horizontal-only blur, width set by per-column theta",
                   subtitle = "left = nadir (crisp) -> right = swath edge (smeared)",
                   ncol = 1),
         "fig2_anisotropy_field.png", w = 9, h = 6)

# Line-spread profile along one row + measured-vs-predicted sigma
prof <- as.matrix(xC_blur, wide = TRUE)[nrC %/% 2, ]
theta_at_bar <- seq(0, 64, length.out = ncC)[bars]
sigma_pred   <- sigma0C / cos(theta_at_bar * pi / 180)^2
sigma_meas   <- vapply(seq_along(bars), function(k) {
  c0 <- bars[k]; win <- max(1, c0 - 30):min(ncC, c0 + 30)
  p  <- prof[win]; d <- win - c0
  sqrt(sum(p * d^2) / sum(p))               # 2nd moment of the local LSF
}, numeric(1))
tab <- data.frame(bar_col = bars, theta_deg = round(theta_at_bar, 1),
                  sigma_pred = round(sigma_pred, 3), sigma_meas = round(sigma_meas, 3))
cat("Line-spread width per bar (predicted = sigma0/cos^2 theta):\n")
print(tab, row.names = FALSE)

dP <- data.frame(column = seq_len(ncC), value = prof)
pC2 <- ggplot(dP, aes(column, value)) +
  geom_area(fill = "#fca50a", alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_line(colour = "#fca50a", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = bars, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Line-spread function along a single row",
       subtitle = "each input bar blurs into a Gaussian whose width grows left -> right",
       x = "cross-track column", y = "blurred value") +
  theme_night()
save_fig(pC2, "fig3_lsf_profile.png", w = 9, h = 3.6)

pC3 <- ggplot(tab, aes(sigma_pred, sigma_meas)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = theta_deg), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "theta (deg)") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Recovered kernel width matches the model",
       subtitle = "measured 2nd moment of each line-spread vs sigma0/cos^2 theta",
       x = expression("predicted " * sigma[x] * " (px)"),
       y = expression("measured " * sigma[x] * " (px)")) +
  theme_night()
save_fig(pC3, "fig4_sigma_validation.png", w = 5.5, h = 5)


# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE D -- the new pool_y argument on a single point source
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE D  |  optional along-track pooling (pool_y)")

nrD <- 120; ncD <- 200
fieldD <- matrix(0, nrD, ncD); fieldD[60, 140] <- 1     # one bright pixel near the edge
xD  <- pix_rast(fieldD)
thD <- make_theta(nrD, ncD, 0, 60)
sig0D <- 2

xD_none <- anisotropic_blur(xD, thD, sigma0 = sig0D, pool_y = "none")
xD_gaus <- anisotropic_blur(xD, thD, sigma0 = sig0D, pool_y = "gaussian", width_y = 5)
xD_unif <- anisotropic_blur(xD, thD, sigma0 = sig0D, pool_y = "uniform",  width_y = 6)

save_fig(gg_panels(list("pool_y = 'none'"            = xD_none,
                        "pool_y = 'gaussian' (sd=5)" = xD_gaus,
                        "pool_y = 'uniform' (+/-6)"  = xD_unif),
                   title = "Point-spread of one pixel under the three pooling modes",
                   subtitle = "x-width set by theta; y handled by pool_y (none = horizontal streak)",
                   ncol = 3),
         "fig5_pool_y.png", w = 12, h = 4.2)


# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE E -- cloud / fill gaps (NA handling)
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE E  |  NA (cloud/fill) gaps are filled, not propagated")

nrE <- 120; ncE <- 240
# simulated city lights: a few Gaussian blobs on a dark field
gx <- matrix(seq_len(ncE), nrE, ncE, byrow = TRUE)
gy <- matrix(seq_len(nrE), nrE, ncE)
blob <- function(cx, cy, a, s) a * exp(-((gx - cx)^2 + (gy - cy)^2) / (2 * s^2))
fieldE <- blob(60, 60, 1, 12) + blob(150, 40, 0.8, 9) + blob(200, 80, 1, 14)
xE_clean <- pix_rast(fieldE)
# punch a cloud: a block + scattered missing pixels
fieldE_na <- fieldE
fieldE_na[30:55, 130:170] <- NA
fieldE_na[sample(length(fieldE_na), 1500)] <- NA
xE_na <- pix_rast(fieldE_na)
thE   <- make_theta(nrE, ncE, 0, 50)

xE_blur <- anisotropic_blur(xE_na, thE, sigma0 = 3, pool_y = "gaussian", width_y = 3)
cat(sprintf("input NA cells = %d   ->   output NA cells = %d\n",
            global(xE_na, fun = "isNA")[1, 1], global(xE_blur, fun = "isNA")[1, 1]))

save_fig(gg_panels(list("input (with cloud gaps)" = xE_na, "blurred (gaps filled)" = xE_blur),
                   title = "NA-aware blur: holes filled from valid neighbours",
                   subtitle = "grey = NA in the input; the num/den step renormalizes per pixel",
                   ncol = 2, limits = c(0, 1)),
         "fig6_na_fill.png", w = 11, h = 3.8)


# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE F -- geometry is preserved (georeferenced raster round-trip)
# =============================================================================
banner("EXAMPLE F  |  extent / CRS / resolution preserved")

geo <- rast(nrows = 80, ncols = 300, xmin = 500000, xmax = 530000,
            ymin = 3200000, ymax = 3208000, crs = "EPSG:32617")  # UTM 17N, metres
values(geo) <- runif(ncell(geo))
thetaG <- geo; values(thetaG) <- rep(seq(0, 55, length.out = ncol(geo)), times = nrow(geo))
geo_blur <- anisotropic_blur(geo, thetaG, sigma0 = 6, pool_y = "gaussian", width_y = 2)
cat(sprintf("ext  in  : %s\n", paste(round(as.vector(ext(geo))), collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("ext  out : %s\n", paste(round(as.vector(ext(geo_blur))), collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("crs match: %s   res match: %s\n",
            crs(geo) == crs(geo_blur), isTRUE(all.equal(res(geo), res(geo_blur)))))

banner(sprintf("DONE.  Figures in:  %s", OUTDIR))

Q: How can I add a label below a QR code and export it to PDF in React? A:

If your requirement is more than just rendering a QR code and you need a reusable way to place labels, text, images, and QR codes together and export them as a print-ready PDF, you may want to look at QR Layout Designer.

Demo: QR Layout Designer Demo

It provides:

  • Drag-and-drop QR label designer

  • Text labels positioned below/around QR codes

  • React integration

  • PDF export with layout preservation

  • PNG and ZPL export support

  • Dynamic data binding ({{name}}, {{id}}, etc.)

Instead of manually combining react-qr-code, html2canvas, and jsPDF, you can design the label visually and export it directly. The generated layout can also be saved as JSON and reused for batch printing.

GitHub: QR Layout Tool Repository

Q: Using RFID Reader on Node JS A:

I know this is a bit late but I'm putting it here just in case someone passed by it.

You are getting this error because you are using a native module which is ok for node, but because electron is a modified node, so in order for thhat to work: you need to rebuild for electron instead:

  • Add the electron-rebuild package npm i -D electron-rebuild
  • Remove the node-modules folder, as well as the packages-lock.json file.
  • Run npm install to install all modules.
  • Run ./node_modules/.bin/electron-rebuild or .\node_modules\.bin\electron-rebuild.cmd for Windows to rebuild everything.
